_comment: AgentFW r9 example permissions + hooks for Claude Code. MERGE these entries into your existing ~/.claude/settings.json (or a project .claude/settings.json) — do NOT replace that file. The agentfw-install tool never modifies settings.json; this merge is a manual step. Adjust paths/branch names to your environment.
_limitations: Honest limit: command-name allowlists cannot express the effects taxonomy. Any allowed file-dumping command (cat/head/awk/base64/...) or code-executing command (test runners, build scripts, interpreters) reopens what the Read denies below close — e.g. a test suite is repository-controlled code that can read ~/.ssh and exfiltrate it. Secrets isolation and egress control therefore need the deny rules PLUS hooks/sandboxing (PreToolUse guards, OS-level sandboxes, network policy) — deny rules alone are pattern-matching, not containment. Treat this file as a starting point to NARROW per project, not as a global grant.

permissions._ask_comment: Test runners and linters sit in ask, not allow: they execute repository-controlled code (arbitrary read + egress under your user), so running them is a per-invocation trust decision, not a standing grant. File reads go through the Read/Glob/Grep tool rules above, which honor the Read denies — shell file-dumpers (cat/find/grep/rg/ls/wc) are deliberately NOT allowed here because they would bypass those denies.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import json,re,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); c=d.get('tool_input',{}).get('command',''); bad=re.search(r'git\s+push\b(?=[^|;&]*(?:--force(?:-with-lease)?|\s-f\b))[^|;&]*\b(main|master|release)\b', c); sys.exit(2 if bad else 0)"
